explain.heart rate: How many times her heart beats each minute. Hers is a little higher than her usual, which can happen in hot weather.
explain.blood pressure: How hard blood pushes on the walls of her arteries. The top number has crept up for 6 weeks, which raises her stroke chance. Taking the evening tablet every day is the simplest fix.
explain.calm score: Also called heart rate variability. Higher means her body is relaxed and recovering; lower means more strain from heat, poor sleep or illness.
explain.sleep: Time actually asleep. She is getting less than usual and waking more at night.
explain.steps: Steps counted by her watch and phone.
explain.walking speed: How fast she walks on flat ground. A slower pace over weeks is one of the best early signs of a higher chance of falling.
explain.tablets: The smart pill box records when each dose is taken.
explain.calls answered: How many of the daily check-in calls she picked up.
explain.speaking pace: Measured during the daily chat. Small changes can be early signs of tiredness, low mood or memory changes.
explain.time with people: Calls, visits and outings with other people.
explain.home temperature: From the sensor in her living room. Above 28° the body works harder, especially with heart conditions.
explain.weight: From her bathroom scale. Sudden gain of 2 kg in 3 days can mean fluid build-up.
explain.pollen: Spring grass pollen. On windy, stormy days it can trigger asthma, even in people who rarely have it.
explain.sun strength: The UV index. 11 is extreme: skin can burn in under 10 minutes.
explain.plane noise: Marrickville is under the airport flight path. Flights stop between 11 pm and 6 am, so her sleep is not affected.
explain.pre-arrival packets: FHIR R4 bundles (Patient, Condition, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Observation) pushed to the ED on escalation, with consent on file.
explain.door to ct: Median minutes from ED arrival to first CT head for suspected stroke, packet-enabled arrivals vs historical baseline.
explain.notice before arrival: Median interval between packet receipt and ambulance arrival at triage.

chatIntro: Mum is steady today. One thing to act on: her blood pressure has drifted up for 6 weeks, and Thursday will be 38 °C.
chatQa: Clear and cheerful at 13:02. Speech rate 132 wpm, a little slower than her usual 141, and she said "pardon?" twice, so captions stay on.
Four drivers: morning blood pressure up 14 mmHg, 3 missed evening doses, two relatives with stroke before 70, and two irregular-rhythm alerts this week. It's a risk level, not a diagnosis.
I'll add a midday check-in, remind her about fluids every 2 hours and offer a lift to the library cool room. Aisha next door can check on her at 15:00.
What should I do this week?
Approve the pill box task for David and book her GP review. Both are one tap. I can also draft a message to Sarah.
